18.290.010 Statement of Intent

The zoning of property as BP, Business Park District, is intended to allow a mix of office, light industrial and limited retail and service uses in a planned business park setting. This district is a planned zoning district designed to provide for low-density, high-quality development with increased amenities and open space; consequently, in appropriate circumstances, property zoned BP may be located adjacent to residential uses.

(History: Ord. ZRR-1725; ZRR-1635)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.290.020 Permitted Uses

No building, structure, land or premises shall be used, and no building or structure shall hereafter be erected, constructed, reconstructed, moved or altered, except for one or more of the following uses, subject to the development and performance standards set forth in Section 18.290.050:

  1. A.
    Any use permitted in District C-0 subject to the applicable development and performance standards.
  2. B.
    Display or catalog showrooms.
  3. C.
    Manufacturing, processing, fabricating or assembling of any commodity except junk or salvage.
  4. D.
    Warehousing, wholesaling or storage of any commodity except junk or salvage.
  5. E.
    Laboratories.
  6. F.
    Printing and publishing.
  7. G.
    Photographic processing facilities.
  8. H.
    Radio and television broadcasting stations.
  9. I.
    Motion picture production and distribution.
  10. J.
    Building and construction contractor services, including display areas.
  11. K.
    Veterinary hospitals and clinics.
  12. L.
    Colleges and universities.
  13. M.
    Business and trade schools.
  14. N.
    Preschools and day care centers.
  15. O.
    Public parks, playgrounds and recreation areas.
  16. P.
    Public or private golf courses, tennis or other courts and swimming pools.
  17. Q.
    Convention centers.
  18. R.
    Auditoriums and conference facilities.
  19. S.
    Commercial pick-up and delivery services.
  20. T.
    Health or exercise clubs.
  21. U.
    Restaurants, not including drive-up or drive-through service.
  22. V.
    Furniture and home furnishings.
  23. W.
    Carpet and floor coverings.
  24. X.
    Paint and wallpaper.
  25. Y.
    Plumbing and electrical supplies.
  26. Z.
    Art galleries and studios.
  27. AA.
    Gymnastic and dance studios.
  28. BB.
    Research establishments of industrial, medical or scientific nature.
  29. CC.
    Sales and installation of cellular phones, stereos, radios and similar electronic equipment for vehicles.
  30. DD.
    The following uses are permitted provided the sales and display floor area shall not exceed 25% of the gross floor area of the main use, and in no event shall such areas exceed 7,500 square feet.
    1. 1.
      Sales of commodities manufactured, processed, fabricated, assembled, warehoused or stored on the premises.
    2. 2.
      Business machines or office supplies; sales and repair.
    3. 3.
      Appliances; sales and repair.
    4. 4.
      Electronics; sales and repair.
  31. EE.
    Post offices and Public Utility Administrative Offices.

     

(History: Ord. ZRR-1865 §1,94; ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.290.030 Height and Area Regulations

The maximum height of buildings and structures and the minimum dimensions of lots and yards shall be as follows, except as otherwise provided in 18.420:

  1. A.
    Maximum height:
    1. 1.
      Buildings -- 40 feet.
    2. 2.
      Structures other than buildings -- 100 feet, provided such structure is set back from all property lines a distance equal to or greater than its height.
  2. B.
    Minimum setbacks:
    1. 1.
      All buildings or structures shall be set back a minimum of 50 feet from any public street right-of-way forming the peripheral property line of the business park.
    2. 2.
      All buildings or structures shall be set back a minimum of 30 feet from any internal street right-of-way.
    3. 3.
      All buildings or structures shall be set back a minimum of 75 feet from the property line of any residentially zoned property, where such property is already developed for residential use or is designated residential on the City's current Future Development Plan.
    4. 4.
      All buildings or structures shall be set back a minimum of 20 feet from any peripheral property line other than a street right-of-way line or residentially zoned property.
    5. 5.
      All buildings or structures shall be set back a minimum of 6 feet from the lot line of any lot within the business park where such lot line does not abut a street right-of-way or the property line of another property other than the business park property.

(History: Ord. ZRR-3373 §32, 2023; Ord. ZRR-1865 §2,94; ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.290.040 Parking and Loading Regulations

  1. A.
    See 18.430 for parking regulations. 
  2. B.
    Each establishment shall provide adequate loading space within a building or in a side or rear yard, in such a way that all storage, standing and maneuvering of trucks shall be off the public right-of-way.

(History: Ord. ZRR-3373 §33, 2023; Ord. ZRR-1865 §3,94; ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.290.050 Development and Performance Standards

  1. A.
    The minimum parcel size of property to be rezoned District BP shall be 15 acres.
  2. B.
    All operations shall be conducted within a fully enclosed building.
  3. C.
    There shall be no outside storage of materials, products or equipment, other than in trash receptacles which must be completely screened utilizing the same building materials as the main building, unless such outside storage is specifically approved as part of the preliminary development plan.
  4. D.
    No use shall be permitted or so operated as to produce or emit from a vent, stack, chimney or combustion process any smoke darker than Ringlemann No. 1, except that smoke darker than Ringlemann No. 2 is permissible for a duration of not more than 4 minutes during any 8-hour period if the source of such emission is not located within 250 feet of residentially zoned property.
  5. E.
    No use may generate any ground-transmitted vibration in excess of .10 inches per second at the property line or in excess of .02 inches per second measured at any residential property line. These values may be multiplied by two for impact vibrations, i.e., discrete vibration pulsations not exceeding 1 second in duration and having a pause of at least 1 second between pulses.
  6. F.
    Outdoor lighting - See 18.435.
  7. G.
    No heat from furnace processing equipment or other device shall be sensed at the lot line or property line to the extent of raising the temperature of air or materials more than 5 degrees Fahrenheit.
  8. H.
    No emission of air contaminants from any source within the boundaries of any lot or tract shall exceed emission rates established by the Kansas Secretary of Health and Environment pursuant to K.S.A. 65-3001 et seq., or amendments thereto, and any administrative regulations adopted thereunder.
  9. I.
    No odor shall be permitted at any lot line or property line exceeding the lowest amount set forth in Table III (Odor Thresholds) of Chapter 5, "Physiological Effects," of the Air Pollution Abatement Manual of the Manufacturing Chemists Association, according to the latest edition of such table for the compounds described therein. For compounds not described in Table III, odor thresholds may be established by methods indicated in Chapter 5 of the manual, and no odor shall be permitted at any lot line or property line exceeding the amount determined by the application of such methods.
  10. J.
    No activity shall be permitted that creates any electrical disturbance that adversely affects any operations or equipment other than those of the creator of such disturbance, or which otherwise causes, creates, or contributes to the interference with electronic signals (including television and radio broadcasting transmissions) to the extent that the operation of any equipment not owned by the creator of such disturbance is adversely affected.
  11. K.
    The minimum landscaped open space ratio for the entire business park shall be .20.
  12. L.
    No loading dock shall be permitted to face any street unless a screening plan therefor is approved as part of final plan approval.

(History: Ord. No. ZRR-3447 §19, 2024; Ord. ZRR-2285 §13, 2001; ZRR-1865 §4,94; ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.300 M-1 Industrial Park District and MP-1 Planned Industrial Park District

18.300.010 Statement of Intent

The zoning of property as M-1, Industrial Park District, or MP-1, Planned Industrial Park District, is intended to provide for light industrial uses, ideally in an industrial park setting. These districts are primarily intended to serve businesses engaged in light manufacturing and related uses, with limited retail and service uses permitted as well.

(History: Ord. ZRR-1725; ZRR-1635)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.300.020 Permitted Uses

No building, structure, land or premises shall be used, and no building or structure shall hereafter be erected, constructed, reconstructed, moved or altered, except for one or more of the following uses, subject to the development and performance standards set forth in Section 18.300.050:

  1. A.
    Manufacturing, processing, fabricating or assembling of any commodity except junk or salvage.
  2. B.
    Warehousing, wholesaling or storage of any commodity except junk or salvage.
  3. C.
    Commercial pick-up and delivery services.
  4. D.
    Laboratories.
  5. E.
    Public and private utility facilities, and governmental maintenance facilities, including the storage and maintenance of motor vehicles and equipment.
  6. F.
    Printing and publishing.
  7. G.
    Appliance repair centers.
  8. H.
    Retail sales of commodities manufactured, processed, fabricated, assembled, warehoused or stored on the premises.
  9. I.
    Commercial bakeries.
  10. J.
    Administrative offices associated with another permitted use.
  11. K.
    Restaurants and automatic food and beverage vending machines.
  12. L.
    Dry cleaning and laundries.
  13. M.
    Pest control services.
  14. N.
    Accessory uses as provided in 18.390.
  15. O.
    Communications Facilities
    1. 1.
      Towers up to a maximum height of 100 feet may permitted administratively; provided, an additional 50 feet to accommodate Collocation may be approved by the Director upon information to the Director's satisfaction certifying the capacity of the tower for two additional providers and an owner’s letter indicating the owner’s intent to share space. A lightning rod, not to exceed 10 feet, shall not be included within these height limitations.
    2. 2.
      Base stations that comply with the same height and setback requirements as other structures in this district.
    3. 3.
      Antennas mounted on existing buildings and water towers.
    4. 4.
      Small Cell/DAS facilities on utility poles or street lights in the public right-of way.
  16. P.
    Utility structures, subject to the requirements outlined in Section 18.250.050(H).
  17. Q.
    Wind turbine, roof-mounted wind turbine(s), and wind turbines mounted on parking lot light poles.
  18. R.
    Lawn care companies.

(History: Ord. ZRR-3134 §22, 2016; ZRR-2914 §1, 2011; ZRR-2836 §12, 2010; ZRR-2262 §12, 2001; ZRR-2004 §7, 96; ZRR-1923 §1, 95; ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637; ZRR-889 §18.30; ZRR-772; ZRR-412)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.300.030 Height and Area Regulations

The maximum height of buildings and structures and the minimum dimensions of lots and yards shall be as follows, except as otherwise provided in 18.420:

  1. A.
    Maximum height:
    1. 1.
      Buildings -- 35 feet.
    2. 2.
      Structures other than buildings -- 100 feet, provided such structure is set back from all property lines a distance equal to or greater than its height.
  2. B.
    Minimum front yard -- 50 feet.
  3. C.
    Minimum side yards:
    1. 1.
      The total of the side yards shall be not less than 40 feet, except that no side yard shall be less than 10 feet.
    2. 2.
      Side yards abutting a street or residentially zoned property shall be not less than 20 feet.
  4. D.
    Minimum rear yard -- 15 feet.

(History: Ord. ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637; ZRR-889 §18.30)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.300.040 Parking and Loading Regulations

  1. A.
    See 18.430 for parking regulations.
  2. B.
    Each establishment shall provide adequate loading space within a building or in a side or rear yard, in such a way that all storage, standing and maneuvering of trucks shall be off the public right-of-way.

(History: Ord. ZRR-3373 §34, 2023; Ord. ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637; ZRR-889 §18.30)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.300.050 Development and Performance Standards

  1. A.
    All operations shall be conducted within a fully enclosed building.
  2. B.
    All storage of materials, products or equipment shall be within a fully enclosed building or in an open yard screened such that the materials, products or equipment are not visible at eye level from adjacent property.
  3. C.
    Areas devoted to retail sales shall not exceed 10% of the gross floor area of the main use, and in no event shall the total of such areas exceed 5,000 square feet.
  4. D.
    No use shall be permitted or so operated as to produce or emit from a vent, stack, chimney or combustion process any smoke darker than Ringlemann No. 1, except that smoke darker than Ringlemann No. 2 is permissible for a duration of not more than four minutes during any 8-hour period if the source of such emission is not located within 250 feet of residentially zoned property.
  5. E.
    No use may generate any ground-transmitted vibration in excess of .10 inches per second at the property line or in excess of .02 inches per second measured at any residential property line. These values may be multiplied by two for impact vibrations, i.e., discrete vibration pulsations not exceeding 1 second in duration and having a pause of at least 1 second between pulses.
  6. F.
    Outdoor lighting - See 18.435.
  7. G.
    No heat from furnace processing equipment or other device shall be sensed at the lot line or property line to the extent of raising the temperature of air or materials more than 5 degrees Fahrenheit.
  8. H.
    No emission of air contaminants from any source within the boundaries of any lot or tract shall exceed emission rates established by the Kansas Secretary of Health and Environment pursuant to K.S.A. 65-3001 et seq., or amendments thereto, and any administrative regulations adopted thereunder.
  9. I.
    No odor shall be permitted at any lot line or property line exceeding the lowest amount set forth in Table III (Odor Thresholds) of Chapter 5, "Physiological Effects," of the Air Pollution Abatement Manual of the Manufacturing Chemists Association, according to the latest edition of such table for the compounds described therein. For compounds not described in Table III, odor thresholds may be established by methods indicated in Chapter 5 of the manual, and no odor shall be permitted at any lot line or property line exceeding the amount determined by the application of such methods.
  10. J.
    No activity shall be permitted that creates any electrical disturbance that adversely affects any operations or equipment other than those of the creator of such disturbance, or which otherwise causes, creates, or contributes to the interference with electronic signals (including television and radio broadcasting transmissions) to the extent that the operation of any equipment not owned by the creator of such disturbance is adversely affected.
  11. K.
    No loading dock shall be permitted to face any street unless a screening plan therefor is approved as part of final plan approval.
  12. L.
    Prior to issuance of any building permit, site plan approval shall be obtained as provided for in 18.140.
  13. M.
    Communications Facilities - Communications facilities are subject to the application, location and performance standards of 18.395 - Communications Facilities.
  14. N.
    A ground-mounted wind turbine is permitted to a maximum height of 100 feet, measured from average grade at the tower base to the highest point of the wind turbine structure, including blades, if applicable. A lightning rod, not to exceed 10 feet, shall not be included within the height limitations. In addition, a ground- or roof-mounted wind turbine shall be subject to the performance standards outlined in 18.370.040. Wind turbines mounted on parking lot light poles shall be subject to the performance standards set out in 18.250.050.

(History: Ord. No. ZRR-3447 §20, 2024; Ord. No. ZRR-3357 §4, 2022; Ord. ZRR-3134 §23, 2016; ZRR-2836 §13, 2010; ZRR-2795 §5, 2009; ZRR-2285 §14, 2001; ZRR-2004 §8, 96; ZRR-1725; ZRR-1635; ZRR-889 §18.30)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.310 M-2 General Industrial District and MP-2 Planned General Industrial District

Contents:
  • 18.310.010 Statement of Intent
  • 18.310.020 Permitted Uses
  • 18.310.030 Height and Area Regulations
  • 18.310.040 Parking and Loading Regulations
  • 18.310.050 Development and Performance Standards

18.310.010 Statement of Intent

The zoning of property as M-2, General Industrial District, or MP-2, Planned General Industrial District, is intended to provide for a broad range of light industrial and commercial uses. These districts are the least restrictive districts allowed within the City.

(History: Ord. ZRR-1725; ZRR-1635)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.310.020 Permitted Uses

No building, structure, land or premises shall be used, and no building or structure shall hereafter be erected, constructed, reconstructed, moved or altered, except for one or more of the following uses, subject to the development and performance standards set forth in Section 18.310.050:

  1. A.
    Any use permitted in District M-1 subject to the applicable development and performance standards.
  2. B.
    Any use permitted in District C-3 subject to the applicable development and performance standards.
  3. C.
    Bottling works.
  4. D.
    Bus barns or lots.
  5. E.
    Carpentry, cabinet or pattern shops.
  6. F.
    Carpet cleaning establishments where the cleaning occurs on the premises.
  7. G.
    Chemical laboratories.
  8. H.
    Cleaning, pressing and dyeing plants.
  9. I.
    Cold storage plants.
  10. J.
    Animal pounds and kennels within an enclosed building.
  11. K.
    Electro-plating works.
  12. L.
    Freight terminals (rail or truck).
  13. M.
    Lumber yards and concrete mixing plants.
  14. N.
    Machine shops.
  15. O.
    Moving, transfer or storage plants.
  16. P.
    Plumbing and sheet metal shops.
  17. Q.
    Railroad yards.
  18. R.
    Sales rooms, yards and service for farm machinery, contractors' equipment and oil well supplies.
  19. S.
    Sign painting or fabrication facilities.
  20. T.
    Taxi and limousine storage and maintenance facilities.
  21. U.
    Accessory uses as provided in 18.390.

(History: Ord. ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637; ZRR-889 §18.32; ZRR-772)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.310.030 Height and Area Regulations

The maximum height of buildings and structures and the minimum dimensions of lots and yards shall be as follows, except as otherwise provided in 18.420:

  1. A.
    Maximum height:
    1. 1.
      Buildings -- 35 feet.
    2. 2.
      Structures other than buildings -- 100 feet, provided such structure is set back from all property lines a distance equal to or greater than its height.
  2. B.
    Minimum front yard -- 30 feet.
  3. C.
    Minimum side yards:
    1. 1.
      The total of the side yards shall be not less than 40 feet, except that no side yard shall be less than 10 feet.
    2. 2.
      Side yards abutting a street or residentially zoned property shall be not less than 20 feet.
  4. D.
    Minimum rear yard -- 20 feet.

(History: Ord. ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637; ZRR-889 §18.32) 

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.310.040 Parking and Loading Regulations

  1. A.
    See 18.430 for parking regulations. 
  2. B.
    Each parking area shall be permanently surfaced and shall be located on the premises or within 300 feet thereof on land zoned for commercial or industrial uses or having a special use permit for such purpose.
  3. C.
    Each establishment shall provide adequate loading space within a building or in a side or rear yard in such a way that all storage, standing and maneuvering of trucks shall be off the public right-of-way.

(History: Ord. ZRR-3373 §35, 2023; Ord. ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637; ZRR-889 §18.32)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.310.050 Development and Performance Standards

  1. A.
    No use shall be permitted or so operated as to produce or emit from a vent, stack, chimney or combustion process any smoke darker than Ringlemann No. 2, except that smoke darker than Ringlemann No. 3 is permissible for a duration of not more than 4 minutes during any 8-hour period if the source of emission is not located within 500 feet of residentially zoned property.
  2. B.
    No use may generate any ground-transmitted vibration in excess of .20 inches per second at the property line or in excess of .02 inches per second measured at any residential property line. These values may be multiplied by two for impact vibrations; i.e., discrete vibration pulsations not exceeding 1 second in duration and having a pause of at least 1 second between pulses.
  3. C.
    Outdoor lighting - See 18.435.
  4. D.
    No heat from furnace processing equipment or other device shall be sensed at the lot line or property line to the extent of raising the temperature of air or materials more than 5 degrees Fahrenheit.
  5. E.
    No emission of air contaminants from any source within the boundaries of any lot or tract shall exceed emission rates established by the Kansas Secretary of Health and Environment pursuant to K.S.A. 65-3001 et seq., or amendments thereto, and any administrative regulations adopted thereunder.
  6. F.
    No odor shall be permitted at any lot line or property line exceeding the lowest amount set forth in Table III (Odor Thresholds) of Chapter 5, "Physiological Effects," of the Air Pollution Abatement Manual of the Manufacturing Chemists Association, according to the latest edition of such table for the compounds described therein. For compounds not described in Table III, odor thresholds may be established by methods indicated in Chapter 5 of the manual, and no odor shall be permitted at any lot line or property line exceeding the amount determined by the application of such methods.
  7. G.
    No activity shall be permitted that creates any electrical disturbance that adversely affects any operations or equipment other than those of the creator of such disturbance, or which otherwise causes, creates, or contributes to the interference with electronic signals (including television and radio broadcasting transmissions) to the extent that the operation of any equipment not owned by the creator of such disturbance is adversely affected.
  8. H.
    Prior to issuance of any building permit, site plan approval shall be obtained as provided for in 18.140.

(History: Ord. No. ZRR-3447 §21, 2024; Ord. ZRR-2285 §15, 2001; ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637; ZRR-889 §18.32)

18.350 MHP Mobile Home Park District

Contents:
  • 18.350.010 Statement of Intent
  • 18.350.020 Permitted Uses
  • 18.350.030 Plan Approval
  • 18.350.040 Area and Setback Requirements
  • 18.350.050 Development and Performance Standards

18.350.010 Statement of Intent

The zoning of property as MHP, Mobile Home Park District, is intended to provide for mobile home parks where such development is appropriate given the surrounding land uses and neighborhood. The MHP district is intended to promote affordable housing consistent with the provisions of the Comprehensive Plan.

(History: Ord. ZRR-3416 §22, 2023; ​​​​​​​Ord. ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.350.020 Permitted Uses

No land or premises shall be used and no structure shall be hereafter erected, constructed, reconstructed, moved or altered except for one or more of the following uses, subject to the development and performance standards set forth in Section 18.350.050:

  1. A.
    Mobile homes;
  2. B.
    Manufactured homes;
  3. C.
    Utility structures, subject to the requirements outlined in Section 18.180.070(H).

(History: Ord. ZRR-2262 §13, 2001; ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.350.030 Plan Approval

Prior to approval of MHP zoning, a development plan for the proposed mobile home park shall be prepared for consideration concurrent with the rezoning application. The plan shall be accurately drawn, at a scale acceptable to the Director of Planning and Development Services, and shall show the following:

  1. 1.
    Proposed street and drive pattern.
  2. 2.
    Proposed mobile/manufactured home spaces and their approximate dimensions.
  3. 3.
    Any existing streets in or abutting the property.
  4. 4.
    Location and size of parking spaces.
  5. 5.
    Location and size of park and playground areas.
  6. 6.
    Location of shelters
  7. 7.
    Screening and landscaping.
  8. 8.
    Legal description of the tract.
  9. 9.
    Name of the landowner, developer and the firm preparing the plan.
  10. 10.
    North point, scale and date.

Five copies of the plan shall be submitted with the rezoning application.

(History: Ord. ZRR-2343 §46, 2002; ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.350.040 Area and Setback Requirements

  1. A.
    All mobile home parks shall have a site area of at least 40 acres.
  2. B.
    Density of mobile home parks shall be not greater than five units per acre.
  3. C.
    All units shall be set back a minimum of 30 feet from the boundary line of the mobile home park and from the right-of-way line of any public street.
  4. D.
    The minimum width of each mobile home space shall be 50 feet.
  5. E.
    The minimum depth of each mobile home space shall be 100 feet.

(History: Ord. ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.350.050 Development and Performance Standards

  1. A.
    No mobile home manufactured on or after September 1, 1973 shall be located in a mobile home park unless such mobile home complies with the provisions of K.S.A. 75-1211 et seq., as amended, and rules and regulations adopted thereunder. No mobile home manufactured prior to September 1, 1973 shall be placed, stored or parked within a mobile home park unless such mobile home is in compliance with applicable provisions of the Building Code.
  2. B.
    Each mobile home space shall contain a portland cement or asphaltic concrete stand upon which the unit will be situated, and each unit shall be equipped with skirts on all sides, such skirts to be of material harmonious to the unit structure and installed within ten days of the unit placement.
  3. C.
    All mobile/manufactured homes installed within the mobile home park shall be anchored to the ground by means of anchors attached both to the frame and with straps extending over the top and completely surrounding the sides and roof. Anchor design shall be approved by the Code Administrator prior to installation and shall comply with all requirements of the State of Kansas. In addition, test data giving certified results of pull tests in soils representative of the area in which the anchors are to be used shall be submitted to the Code Administrator. Minimum load in direct pull shall be 5,400 pounds. Anchors shall be marked so that after installation, the identification is in plain view for inspection.
  4. D.
    Each mobile home park shall provide sufficient and adequate number of shelters from natural disasters. Shelters shall be placed at such intervals within the park to ensure maximum safety for residents during times of natural disasters. Design and location of such shelters shall be determined at the time of plan approval, but in no case shall the construction of the initial phase of a mobile home park be allowed to proceed without the concurrent construction of appropriate shelters.
  5. E.
    All streets within the park shall be improved to City standards for residential streets. There shall be at least two street or drive openings into the park providing ingress and egress. All private drives shall be not less than 24 feet in width, having portland cement curbs, and be surfaced with at least six inches of compacted stone base with two inches of hot mix bituminous concrete as the surface course, or the equivalent, as determined by the City Engineer.
  6. F.
    At least two parking spaces for each mobile/manufactured home shall be provided within 60 feet of the unit. Such parking spaces shall be off the public street or private drive, and each shall be not less than 9 feet by 20 feet in size, and shall be surfaced to at least the standards set forth above for private drives.
  7. G.
    Each mobile/manufactured home shall be located on the mobile home space so that no part of one home structure, including canopies, awnings, carports and other protrusions, is closer than 12 feet to another home, or to the edge of the surface of a drive. Each mobile home space shall have not less than two live trees of two to two and one-half inch caliper in such open space area.
  8. H.
    Park and playground space shall be provided for occupants of the mobile home park on the basis of 300 square feet for each space in the park. Such playground space shall be separate and in addition to the open space required for each mobile home space, and shall be equipped and maintained for the use of the residents of the park.
  9. I.
    All liquid wastes shall be disposed of through a sanitary sewer system and treatment facility, the plans of which shall be approved by the City Engineer prior to construction. All solid waste shall be disposed of by accumulation in tight containers, and removed at regular intervals.
  10. J.
    All power and telephone lines shall be underground and shall be in compliance with standards of the utility corporation involved.
  11. K.
    The site of the park shall be graded so that surface water will not accumulate, but will run off in a manner that will not adversely affect the residential character of the park or adjacent property. The proposed drainage system shall be approved by the City Engineer prior to construction of streets or other portions of the park.
  12. L.
    Each mobile home park shall have a resident manager and shall be operated in a sanitary, orderly and efficient manner, and shall maintain a neat appearance at all times. Suitable and effective rules for regulating the outside storage of equipment, the removal of wheels and installation of skirtings, the collection of trash and garbage, and the attachment of appurtenances to the unit shall be continually enforced. All portions of the mobile home park shall be open and accessible to fire, police and other emergency and protective vehicles and personnel, including city, county and state inspectors. A map shall be placed at the main entrance to the park, clearly showing the location of each space, and the name and address of the occupant. Such map shall be illuminated at all times and be enclosed in a weatherproof case within full view of persons entering the park.

(History: Ord. ZRR-1725; ZRR-1637)

Effective on: 1/1/1901

18.360 Floodplain Management Ordinance
